channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler zero-days exploited for weeks before disclosure, CISA warns
item.description: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, are being exploited worldwide. New reporting from Tenable and other researchers indicates attackers had been inside vulnerable appliances for weeks before the public disclosure, not days. The unauthenticated flaw lets an attacker run commands on a default configuration; the second is a memory-overflow bug reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the default on virtual VPN servers. Investigators found a uniquely generated webshell on each compromised device, and assess the activity as likely nation-state espionage. The Dutch NCSC and CISA both confirmed exploitation and added the flaws to KEV with a 30 September deadline. Shadowserver counts about 23,000 internet-exposed appliances, and Citrix warns that indicators may have limited forensic value, so preserve evidence before patching. NetScaler commonly fronts remote-access paths into OT environments, making every unpatched appliance a live foothold. - Citrix security bulletin CTX697096; CISA KEV catalog and 27 Sep alert (30 Sep deadline); Dutch NCSC; Tenable and Rapid7 research; reported by Help Net Security, BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek - Exploited for weeks before disclosure; Citrix confirmed and patched 27 Sep 2026; added to CISA KEV 27 Sep 2026 (federal deadline 30 Sep 2026)

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers altered pumps and disabled alarms at two small water systems
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no new development since disclosure
item.description: Colorado Governor Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote alarms and altering pumping cycles. Officials describe the disruption as brief, with no known impact to treatment, water quality or public safety, and say they cannot yet confirm which foreign actors were responsible. A separately tracked, broader Iran-linked campaign against US water systems has not been formally connected to this incident. It remains the only confirmed case of OT tampering in this edition, with nothing new reported since the initial disclosure. - Colorado Governor’s office statement, reported by Industrial Cyber, Axios Denver and SecurityWeek - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of this edition

item.title: [High] A third vessel’s hijacked-valve claim stays unverified as a Texas regulator urges operators to harden defenses
item.category: Incident — Coast Guard- and FBI-confirmed cyber intrusions on two Galveston-bound tankers boarded in August; a third vessel’s (LNG carrier) crew claim of a hijacked safety system unverified by any maritime authority; a Texas regulator cites the boardings in a public statement; no confirmed shore-side disruption
item.description: The Coast Guard and FBI boarded the tanker VL Prosperity off Galveston on 21 August and a second US-bound tanker on 24 August, with Rear Admiral Amy Grable confirming investigators found evidence of a malicious cyber actor on the vessels’ IT and other onboard systems; neither ship was found unsafe to operate, and the Coast Guard has not publicly attributed the intrusions to Iran despite Iranian state media claiming credit. A third vessel, the LNG carrier Vivit Africa, reported a suspected cyberattack near the Strait of Gibraltar in September; its crew alleged attackers briefly took control of tank-pressure and relief-valve systems, but the Italian Coast Guard and Korean Register have confirmed only a systems malfunction, not a cyberattack. On 24 September, Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a public statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to strengthen their cyber defenses. - US Coast Guard and FBI statements, reported by SecurityWeek and CBS News; Cybernews reporting on the Vivit Africa claim; Railroad Commission of Texas statement via WorldOil - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; Vivit Africa claim reported 21 Sep, updated 24 Sep; Texas statement 24 Sep 2026 — no official development since

item.title: [Critical] Chained flaws in an IO-Link master hand an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor data
item.category: Research — CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014: 18 CVEs across Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3 IO-Link masters, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass and a persistent command-injection flaw; chainable for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation
item.description: CERT@VDE disclosed 18 vulnerabilities in Pepperl+Fuchs’s ICE2 and ICE3 series IO-Link masters on 16 September in advisory VDE-2026-014. The worst, CVE-2026-27546, is an authentication bypass scored CVSS 9.8; a companion flaw, CVE-2026-27565, lets an attacker inject operating-system commands through a malicious IODD file upload that persists after reboot. Chained together, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover. - CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014 - Published 16 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Forescout: only 13% of OT network segments are actually OT-only
item.category: Research — Forescout analysis of 47,700 network segments across 209 organizations; only 13% of OT-containing segments are dedicated exclusively to OT (6% for medical-only segments); sector-aggregated statistics, not a specific incident; no CVE
item.description: Forescout examined 47,700 network segments holding more than 2.5 million devices across 209 organizations, publishing findings on 22 September. Just 13% of segments containing OT devices were dedicated exclusively to OT, and only 6% of medical-device segments were isolated solely for that equipment; the average segment held 54 devices across four device categories. The researchers conclude that OT and medical devices routinely share network space with general enterprise assets, widening the blast radius available to an attacker who lands anywhere on a converged network — a structural exposure rather than an active campaign. - Forescout Research (Vedere Labs), reported by SecurityWeek - Published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Ransomware volume hit a 2026 high in August, and industrial organizations took roughly a third of it
item.category: Threat intel — NCC Group’s August 2026 ransomware review counts 1,073 attacks, up 12% on July, with the industrial sector the target in about 31%; Qilin leads; no CVE
item.description: NCC Group’s review of August 2026, reported by Industrial Cyber on 28 September, recorded 1,073 ransomware attacks, a 12% rise on July. Industrial organizations were the target in 329 of them (31%), and North America took 44% of all victims. Qilin was the most active operator with 164 incidents (15%), overtaking The Gentlemen. The report also flags Aurora, a ransomware-as-a-service group active since late April that goes after manufacturing and transport using VPN exploitation, credential harvesting and hypervisor encryption — the same remote-access edge covered elsewhere in this edition. These are victim-leak-site counts, so they measure claimed attacks rather than confirmed operational shutdowns. - NCC Group monthly threat report, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 28 Sep 2026; covers August 2026 activity

item.title: [Medium] Infostealer logs show stolen logins at nearly 1,800 US water utilities, including one meter vendor tied to about 167
item.category: Threat intel — SpyCloud study finds active infostealer exposure at 1,787 of about 10,000 EPA-registered water systems; identity data only, no confirmed intrusion; no CVE
item.description: SpyCloud examined roughly 10,000 EPA-registered water and wastewater organizations and found 1,787 with active infostealer exposure, meaning credentials harvested from infected devices are circulating. In one case, a single infected device at a smart-meter technology provider held logins for about 167 utility customers, a supply-chain multiplier. Of the affected organizations, 258 had credentials tied to OT or remote-access systems. The research covers identity data, not utilities’ control devices, and does not show that anyone used the credentials to break in. It arrives days after Colorado’s confirmed water intrusions, where the access method remains undisclosed. - SpyCloud research, reported by CyberScoop - Reported 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Check Point’s federal patch deadline has passed for two exploited flaws spanning the VPN gateway and the server that manages it
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway/Spark VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers/SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 now passed
item.description: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two separate flaws now past their federal remediation deadline. CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate-validation issue on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls running site-to-site or remote-access VPN, allows unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal affecting Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and run scripts. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September alongside flaws in Arista VeloCloud and F5 BIG-IP APM; the 25 September deadline has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small, unmanned sites. - Check Point security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; reported by BleepingComputer and Help Net Security - Exploitation confirmed by 22 Sep 2026; KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed

item.title: [Critical] A broken authentication check in Schneider’s flagship M580 safety PLC needs a validated patch window
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-3869 (CVSS v4 9.2), Schneider Electric Modicon M580, M580 Safety and MC80 PLCs; incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm; fixed firmware available (SEVD-2026-251-04), no known exploitation
item.description: Schneider Electric disclosed CVE-2026-3869 on 9 September in advisory SEVD-2026-251-04: an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm affecting Modicon M580 controllers below application level 4.00, M580 Safety below 4.20, and Modicon MC80 units. The flaw scores CVSS v4 9.2 and could let an attacker who reaches the controller bypass authentication on management functions. The M580 is Schneider’s flagship PLC platform, deployed widely across process manufacturing, water, oil and gas and power applications, and the Safety variant runs safety-instrumented functions tied directly to process protection. No exploitation has been reported, and fixed firmware is available, but like most safety-certified controllers it can’t be patched without a validated change-control cycle, so unpatched units are likely to stay in service for weeks or months — making network isolation the interim control that matters most. - Schneider Electric advisory SEVD-2026-251-04; CVE-2026-3869 public record - Published 9 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A critical bug in the lwIP network stack embedded in countless controllers and gateways lets an attacker run code remotely
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-265-01: out-of-bounds write in the lwIP embedded TCP/IP stack’s MQTT client, CVE-2026-87121, CVSS 9.8; public proof-of-concept reported; not in CISA KEV
item.description: CISA published advisory ICSA-26-265-01 on 22 September for CVE-2026-87121 (CVSS 9.8), an out-of-bounds write in the MQTT client component of lwIP, a widely embedded open-source TCP/IP stack. An unauthenticated network attacker could gain code execution on a device that uses the vulnerable MQTT client. Because lwIP ships inside many vendors’ firmware, exposure depends on whether a given product enables the MQTT client and which vendor has issued a rebuilt image. A public proof-of-concept has been reported, but the flaw is not in CISA’s exploited-vulnerabilities catalog and no in-the-wild use is confirmed. Asset owners will mostly be waiting on their device vendors. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-265-01; corroborated by CVE record aggregators - Advisory published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
item.category: Guidance — FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion
item.description: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk on 24 September, prompted by a prior compromise of a US industrial automation company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. The agencies say intruders searched the company’s systems for terms like “customers” and “SCADA” and staged customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; downstream customers referenced in the guidance include power utilities and transportation entities. The guidance recommends least-privilege integrator access, on-demand and auditable remote sessions, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security terms in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if an integrator is compromised. - FBI and CISA joint fact sheet; reported by Industrial Cyber - Released 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — comments are open until 30 November
item.category: Guidance — NIST releases initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security”; expanded sector scope, restructured around CSF 2.0; comment period through 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail and maritime vessels; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026, and it lands the same week as the FBI/CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above). - NIST Computer Security Resource Center; reported by SecurityWeek and Industrial Cyber - Draft published 21 Sep 2026; comments due 30 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] FERC approves CIP-014-4, tightening physical-security risk assessments for critical transmission substations
item.category: Regulation — FERC approves NERC CIP-014-4 (transmission physical security); effective 1 Oct 2028; no CVE
item.description: FERC approved NERC’s CIP-014-4 on 16 September, revising the transmission physical-security standard. The update merges two separate review periods into a single 36-month cycle, brings jointly owned transmission facilities into scope, requires steady-state and dynamic simulations under peak and off-peak load cases, and has owners identify facilities within 1,500 feet of critical infrastructure. It takes effect 1 October 2028 and covers roughly 344 transmission owners. Although it is a physical-security standard, the same substations and control houses are OT cyber targets, so assessments should be aligned with CIP-002 and CIP-013 work. - FERC order on NERC CIP-014-4; reported by Industrial Cyber - Approved 16 Sep 2026; effective 1 Oct 2028
